Orsted AS Emerges from Insolvency, Resumes Operations After Court-Supervised Process

Copenhagen — Denmark’s electric utilities sector saw a major development this week as Orsted AS concluded its court-supervised insolvency process, allowing the company to resume normal operations after weeks of uncertainty. The insolvency, which was initiated last month due to “severe liquidity pressures” following project delays and rising costs, has been resolved through a restructuring agreement approved by the Copenhagen District Court.

According to a statement from Orsted AS, the company’s core generation assets remained operational throughout the proceedings, but key supply chain activities and several offshore wind projects were temporarily halted. With the court’s approval, Orsted AS has restructured its outstanding debts and secured a new credit facility from a consortium of Danish lenders, led by Nordholm Bank. “We are grateful for the swift cooperation of our stakeholders, which enabled us to protect our essential services and workforce,” said acting CEO Lars Mikkelsen. “We are now focused on stabilizing our operations and delivering on our commitments to customers and partners.”

Industry analysts say the resolution averts wider disruptions in Denmark’s green energy transition. “A disorderly collapse of Orsted AS would have sent shockwaves through the entire sector,” noted Helena Vestergaard, energy analyst at Dansk Markets Insight. Union representatives acknowledged anxiety among employees but welcomed the continuity agreement. “Safeguarding jobs was our top priority,” stated Birgitte Sørensen of the Danish Energy Workers Union.

Orsted AS shares, which had been suspended during the insolvency process, are set to resume trading on the Copenhagen Stock Exchange later this week. The company indicated that all suspended operations are now being brought back online.
